question.text: This is the collective name given to Aboriginals who were taken from their families and forced to assimilate into white society. In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to this group.
question.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

swap.text: Academics from this country, the home of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, fight "history wars" over the legacy of its colonization by the First Fleet.
swap.clue: One criminal from this country fashioned his own suit of armor and got besieged at Glenrowan.

question.text: This man has hidden in an Ecuadorian embassy since 2012, a saga stemming from sexual assault charges now dropped. His 2010 talk was "Why the World Needs Wikileaks".
question.clue: Daniel Ellsberg praised this man, saying his actions were similar to Ellsberg's handling of the Pentagon Papers.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the only successful armed uprising in Australian history.
swap.text: Major George Johnston invaded Government House and placed Bligh under arrest in this capital city of New South Wales.
swap.clue: This city is the largest to be served by the Snowy Mountains Hydroelectric Scheme, whose construction caused its country to ease pro-white immigration policies.

question.leadin: Malcolm Fraser came to power after a 1975 constitutional crisis in Australia.
question.text: Fraser succeeded Gough (goff) Whitlam, the leader of this political party, which shares its name, but not its American-style spelling, with one of the two main parties in the U.K.
question.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

swap.text: Unfortunately for him, Disraeli wouldn't be prime minister forever, especially after his retired rival William Gladstone led the Midlothian Campaign against him which helped this party retake parliament.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party (do NOT accept or prompt on “Labour” as this that did not exist yet)
swap.clue: A faction led by Robert Peel's followers combined with the Whigs to form this party, whose members included Herbert Asquith.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a World War I battle.
question.text: This military group, composed of soldiers from two nations, landed at Gallipoli at its namesake cove, but was disbanded after the campaign's failure.
question.answer: Australian and New Zealand Army Corps
question.clue: Alexander Godley collaborated with William Birdwood to oversee its operations, which didn't formally cease until another branch of it disbanded after Villers-Bretonneux.

swap.leadin: Name some things about possibly the world's funniest military misadventure.
swap.text: In this brief one month war, Major G. P. W. Meredith failed in his mission to exterminate a namesake avian population despite having machine guns.
swap.clue: One side in this war was targeted because they kept creating gaps in rabbit fences.

question.leadin: In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to the Stolen Generation, who were children of these people that were forcibly taken from their families.
question.text: Name these indigenous people of Australia.
question.clue: Over two dozen of these people were killed in the Myall Creek Massacre, which took place not long after the Black War against these people.

swap.text: This Australian bushranger, who committed several murders at Stringybark Creek, made a homemade suit of bulletproof armor for his final shootout with the police at Glenrowan.
swap.clue: This man sent a lewd note wrapped around calves' testicles to Jeremiah McCormack's wife.

question.text: William Bligh was overthrown as Governor of New South Wales in this rebellion, which resulted from his attempts to curtail trade of its namesake liquor. This rebellion was led by John Macarthur and George Johnston.
question.clue: George Johnston met up with John Macarthur, the wealthy merchant for whom the warrant had been issued, and together they raised an army to storm the Government House.

swap.leadin: Identify some things about the geography of Australia.
swap.text: This tallest mountain in Australia takes its name from a similar peak in Poland, which is named after a Polish hero of the American Revolutionary War.

question.leadin: Following this man's death, a Memorial Swimming Centre was opened in his name.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister, who drowned while swimming off Cheviot Beach in rough conditions. One ridiculous conspiracy theory claimed a Chinese submarine had picked him up.
question.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

swap.leadin: A 1920 act titled "Protection of" [this word] bans using this word for commercial purposes, except when referring to its namesake oatmeal coconut "biscuits."
swap.text: What word names an April 25th holiday that commemorates the amphibious landing of an Army Corps made up of forces from two Commonwealth countries, as well as the cove where they landed?
swap.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

question.leadin: Two accounts by the sailor Watkin Tench are important sources for the early history of this colony, whose European settlers arrived on the First Fleet.
question.text: Name this colony to which British, Irish, and African convicts were transported in order to populate the new city of Sydney.
question.answerHtml: New South Wales [or NSW; accept Botany Bay; accept Port Jackson; prompt on Australia]
question.clue: The Tenterfield Oration, calling for states to unify for purposes of defense, was given in this state, which was also the landing spot for Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet.

swap.leadin: These people's first recorded interaction with outsiders are with the Macassans, who went on trepanging ("treh-PANG-ing") expeditions to their country's coast.
swap.text: Name these people, whose Yolngu ("YOLE-ngoo") subgroup recorded such interaction in rock art. These people's "X-ray" rock art technique can be seen at Ubirr in Kakadu National Park.
swap.clue: That report documented a policy of taking children of these people and bringing them up in white culture.

question.text: Lindqvist recounted the mistreatment of Aboriginal Australians in a 2007 book titled for this phrase. This two-word Latin phrase names a legal doctrine used to justify colonization that was rejected by the Mabo case.
question.answerHtml: terra nullius [accept terrae nullius; accept Terra Nullius: A Journey Through No One’s Land]

swap.text: While charting the coast of Arnhem Land, this explorer encountered a Makassan trepang fleet led by chief Pobasso. This Royal Navy officer is credited as the first person to use the name Australia.
swap.clue: This explorer was a member of William Bligh's Second Breadfruit Voyage that successfully brought the crop to the Caribbean.

question.text: During the Second Boer War, this Australian soldier was court-martialed and executed for his summary execution of Boer prisoners and the murder of a German missionary. He is a folk hero for some Australians.
question.clue: George Witton's book Scapegoats of the Empire claimed that this man's most famous action, before which he told his men to "give no quarter", was done in retaliation for the death of a commander of a raid that launched from Devil's Gorge, named Percy Hunt.

swap.text: This politician alleged that Packer nearly had him killed in the 1980s. This Australian prime minister of the 2010s came to prominence by leading the "Yes" coalition in the 1999 republic referendum.
